propositions.text: Claimant seeks refugee protection under ss 96 and 97(1) of IRPA.
propositions.quote: XXXXX XXXXX, the claimant, seeks refugee protection under ss 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

propositions.text: All evidence, counsel's submissions and Tribunal Officer's representations were received and carefully considered.
propositions.quote: All of the evidence submitted and counsel's submissions and the Tribunal Officer's representations were received and carefully considered.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant seeks refugee protection under IRPA ss 96 and 97(1), and all evidence and submissions were carefully considered by the tribunal.

propositions.text: Claimant is not a Convention refugee as he lacks well-founded fear of persecution in UAE.
propositions.quote: I find that the claimant is not a Convention refugee because he does not have a well-founded fear of persecution for a Convention ground in United Arab Emirates

propositions.text: Claimant is not a person in need of protection; removal to UAE would not risk life, cruel treatment, or torture.
propositions.quote: I also find that the claimant is not a person in need of protection, in that his removal to United Arab Emirates would not subject him personally to a risk to his life, or to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment, and that there are no substantial grounds to believe that his removal to United Arab Emirates will subject him personally to a danger of torture.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal finds claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor in need of protection from removal to UAE.

propositions.text: Summary of claimant's allegations from second Personal Information Form (PIF).
propositions.quote: The following is a summary of the claimant's allegations from the narrative of his second Personal Information Form (PIF).

propositions.text: Claimant alleges claim should be heard against Lebanon due to travel document from there.
propositions.quote: He alleged his claim should be heard against Lebanon, since he has a travel document from that country.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges his claim should be heard against Lebanon due to his travel document, as summarized from his second PIF.

propositions.text: Claimant's life was comfortable in UAE until 2007 when his friend was arrested by state security.
propositions.quote: The claimant said his life was very comfortable in United Arab Emirates until XXXXX XXXXX, 2007, when his best friend, XXXXX XXXXX - XXXXX, a stateless Palestinian, was arrested by state security.

propositions.text: Claimant was questioned three times about his friend and Hamas membership.
propositions.quote: The claimant said he was questioned by state security, three times, regarding his friend and whether his friend was a member of Hamas.

propositions.text: Claimant noticed surveillance and family suggested he go to Canada for safety.
propositions.quote: He said he noticed that he was under surveillance and his family suggested he go to Canada because his life might be at risk.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant alleges comfortable life in UAE until 2007 friend arrest, was questioned thrice, noticed surveillance, and family advised fleeing to Canada.

propositions.text: Claimant has no rights in UAE and cannot stay without a sponsor; came to Canada in 2007 and claimed refugee status same day.
propositions.quote: The claimant said he has no rights in UAE and cannot stay there without a sponsor. He came to Canada on XXXXX XXXXX, 2007 and made his claim the same day.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant says he has no rights or sponsor in UAE, came to Canada in 2007, and claimed refugee protection immediately.

propositions.text: First narrative did not mention UAE problems; lawyer forbade inclusion; residency permit expired in 2007; father laid off; claimant would face human rights violations in refugee camp.
propositions.quote: The claimant's first narrative2 does not mention any problems in United Arab Emirates. He said his first lawyer would not permit this to be included in his narrative. The first narrative said his residency permit for UAE expired on XXXXX XXXXX, 2007. He said his father had been laid off the previous XXXXX, and that, as a stateless descendant of a Palestinian family, he would have to live in a refugee camp there and his human rights would be violated and he would be killed.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant says first narrative omitted UAE problems due to lawyer's advice; residency permit expired; father laid off; risk of human rights violations in refugee camp.

propositions.text: Claimant's personal identity established by travel document and birth certificate.
propositions.quote: The claimant's personal identity is established by his travel document3 and birth certificate.4 I find that the claimant has established his personal identity.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal finds claimant's personal identity established by travel document and birth certificate.

propositions.text: Claimant born and lived in UAE; father left Lebanon refugee camp in 1972 to seek employment; father married mother in UAE; siblings born in UAE.
propositions.quote: The claimant was born in and lived his whole life in United Arab Emirates. He said his father left the refugee camp in Lebanon, where the whole family lived, on XXXXX XXXXX, 1972 and went to XXXXX XXXXX to seek employment. The claimant's father married his mother there and he and all his siblings were born in UAE.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant was born and lived in UAE; father left Lebanon refugee camp in 1972, married mother in UAE; siblings born there too.

propositions.text: Claimant's citizenship is complicated; he came to Canada using Lebanese document that expired before hearing; claimant says he is stateless Palestinian.
propositions.quote: The question of his citizenship, or lack thereof, requires further analysis. The claimant came to Canada using a Lebanese document.5 It expired on XXXXX XXXXX 2009 before the claim was scheduled to be heard. The claimant said he is a stateless Palestinian.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's citizenship is complicated; he used an expired Lebanese document to come to Canada and claims stateless Palestinian status.

propositions.text: Claimant's father was not Lebanese citizen but refugee; Lebanon citizenship law requires Lebanese father for citizenship by descent; naturalization requires decree from Council of Ministers.
propositions.quote: Although the claimant's father came from Lebanon, he was not a citizen there and was a refugee living in a refugee camp. The Lebanon Citizenship Law states that citizenship in Lebanon is acquired as follows:6 * BY BIRTH: Birth within the Republic of Lebanon does not confer citizenship. * BY DESCENT: A child whose father is a citizen of Lebanon is considered to be a Lebanese citizen. A child born in Lebanon to a foreign mother, without acknowledgement by a Lebanese father, obtains the nationality of the mother. All children of Lebanese descent born outside of Lebanon must be registered at the Lebanese embassy or the child's Lebanese citizenship will not be automatically granted. * BY NATURALIZATION: Lebanese citizenship can be acquired by fulfilling the following condition: Person has applied for, and been granted, a Decree from the Lebanese Council of Ministers. Naturalized citizenship cannot otherwise be acquired.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's father was a Lebanese refugee, not citizen; Lebanese citizenship law requires Lebanese father or naturalization decree for citizenship.

propositions.text: UAE residence permits are temporary, issued via employment or family sponsorship; family sponsorship allows residence but not work; permits cancelled if absent over six months.
propositions.quote: I have also considered the evidence adduced regarding what rights a temporary residency permit confers on a person born and raised in UAE. I note from the documents7 as follows: Residence permits in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) are issued through "employment or family sponsorship" on a temporary basis. UAE permits issued via employment sponsorship are issued to individuals who have been sponsored by a local company for employment purposes. Such individuals can reside and work in the UAE for a specified period of time, and, through family sponsorship, can sponsor members of their family to obtain residence permits. However, persons who acquire residence permits via family sponsorship are only able to reside in the country and are not permitted to work. Persons who have a valid UAE residence permit and are residing in the country with their parents who are also holders of valid UAE residence permits, may, upon reaching the age of 18 years, obtain a residence permit on the following conditions: - If the applicant obtains employment in the UAE, whereby the employer would obtain for the applicant, a work/residence permit - If the applicant is a student studying abroad and has presented a certificate to that affect [which has been] authenticated by [a] UAE Embassy, the parents as sponsors would be able to obtain a residence permit for their son/daughter. - If the applicant is a student studying in any UAE University in the United Arab Emirates, the parents as sponsors would be able to obtain a residence permit for their son/daughter. Residence permit holders have the right to re-enter the UAE as often as desired, provided that they do not remain out of the country for an uninterrupted period extending six months. Residence permits are cancelled when permit holders remain out of the UAE for an uninterrupted period longer than six months.

paragraphs.summary: UAE residence permits are temporary, via employment or family sponsorship, with conditions and cancellation after six months absence.

propositions.text: Claimant's evidence aligns with information that UAE residency permits are issued via employment or parental sponsorship under certain conditions.
propositions.quote: The claimant's evidence is consistent with the Response to Information Request quoted above that indicates that UAE residency permits are issued via employment sponsorship through local companies and under parental sponsorship if the potential permit holder is over the age of 18, studying abroad or studying at any UAE University in the United Arab Emirates.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's evidence matches that UAE residency permits are issued via employment or parental sponsorship under specified conditions.

propositions.text: Claimant's temporary residency permit expired before leaving UAE; father lost job and could not sponsor; claimant over 18, not in university, no employer sponsor; permit renewal not possible.
propositions.quote: The claimant's temporary residency permit expired before he left the country. He said his father was let go from his job in XXXXX 2007 and would lose his own temporary resident permit when it expired and could not sponsor him. The claimant was over the age of 18, not registered in a UAE university to obtain a university sponsorship and did not have an employer sponsor. Therefore, he did not qualify to have his permit renewed after its termination date.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's UAE residency permit expired; father lost job and could not sponsor; claimant over 18, not in university, no employer sponsor; no renewal possible.

propositions.text: Claimant has UAE birth certificate but no citizenship; has been out of UAE over six months.
propositions.quote: The claimant has a birth certificate establishing his birth in United Arab Emirates. However, it is clear from his testimony and the documents that he does not have citizenship. Furthermore, he has been out of the country for more than six months.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant has UAE birth certificate but no citizenship and has been outside UAE for over six months.

propositions.text: Claimant was not permanent resident or citizen of UAE when he came to Canada and claimed refugee status.
propositions.quote: I find that the claimant was not a permanent resident or citizen of UAE when he came to Canada and he made his refugee claim.

propositions.text: Claimant's affiliation is only to UAE; he is stateless; UAE is country of former habitual residence and only country for fear of persecution claim.
propositions.quote: His affiliation is clearly only to UAE, where he was born, educated and lived with his parents until he came to Canada. I find he is a stateless person and that his country of former habitual residence is United Arab Emirates. I also find that United Arab Emirates is the only country against which the claimant's fear of persecution will be heard.

propositions.text: Claimant's counsel agreed UAE is only country for fear of persecution claim.
propositions.quote: This was agreed to by the claimant's counsel at the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: Tribunal finds claimant stateless, affiliated only to UAE, which is the only country for his fear of persecution claim, as agreed by counsel.

propositions.text: Determinative issue is whether claimant has objective basis for claim and if state protection exists in UAE if returned.
propositions.quote: The determinative issue in the case now is whether there is an objective basis to the claim today and, if there is, would there be state protection for the claimant if he returned to United Arab Emirates.

paragraphs.summary: The key issue is whether claimant has objective basis for claim and if UAE state protection exists upon return.

propositions.text: Past persecution is not required for a valid fear of persecution on return.
propositions.quote: Past persecution does not have to have occurred for a person to have a valid fear of persecution on return.

paragraphs.summary: Past persecution is not necessary to establish a valid fear of persecution on return, as a legal principle.

propositions.text: Claimant had no problems in UAE except three interrogations about friend arrested in 2007.
propositions.quote: The claimant did not indicate that he had problems while in United Arab Emirates, except for the three interrogations about his lifelong friend who had been arrested on XXXXX XXXXX, 2007, which took place in XXXXX, XXXXX and XXXXX 2007.

propositions.text: Claimant was asked about Hamas and friends; gave no information; unsure if others were questioned.
propositions.quote: He said he was asked if his friend spoke of Hamas at all, and who his other friends were. The claimant said he gave no information because he had nothing to tell them. He was asked and said he did not know if any other friends or his friend's parents were questioned.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant alleges only three interrogations in UAE about friend and Hamas, gave no info, unsure if others questioned.

propositions.text: Claimant felt followed after interrogations; government officials visited parents once; parents said claimant left for US school; no other enquiries.
propositions.quote: He said he felt he was followed after that. He said that after he left the country, government officials went to his parents' home on one occasion, in XXXXX or XXXXX 2007, and his parents told them he had left the country to go to school in the United States. He said that was the only time there was any enquiry.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant felt followed post-interrogations; officials visited parents once who said claimant left for US school; no further enquiries.

propositions.text: Claimant did not mention UAE in first PIF or Immigration interview due to first lawyer's advice; pursuing complaint against lawyer.
propositions.quote: The claimant was asked why there was not mention of UAE in his first PIF, or when he was interviewed at Immigration, and he said that he followed his first lawyer's advice. He also said he has pursued a complaint against that lawyer because of this wrong guidance.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant omitted UAE in first PIF and Immigration interview per first lawyer's advice and is pursuing complaint against that lawyer.

propositions.text: The claimant did not exaggerate problems in UAE in second PIF or oral testimony
propositions.quote: The claimant did not exaggerate the problems he had in UAE either in his second PIF or in oral testimony.

propositions.text: No negative credibility inference drawn from inconsistent testimony about fears in Lebanon and UAE
propositions.quote: I am prepared to give him the benefit of the doubt and do not draw a negative credibility inference from his inconsistent testimony about his fears in Lebanon, as well as UAE.

propositions.text: Claimant is stateless and UAE is country of former habitual residence, so focus is on fear of persecution there
propositions.quote: since I find that he is stateless and his country of former habitual residence is United Arab Emirates, I am concerned only with his fear of persecution there.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant did not exaggerate UAE problems, gives benefit of doubt on inconsistent fears, and focuses on UAE fear of persecution.

propositions.text: No evidence claimant is of interest to government now due to no enquiries in 2.5 years
propositions.quote: There is no evidence that he is of interest to the government today, since there have been no enquiries about him in two-and-a-half years.

propositions.text: Claimant's past experience was harassment, not persecution
propositions.quote: I find what he experienced was unfortunate but was harassment only and not persecution.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no current government interest in claimant and that past harassment was not persecution.

propositions.text: As stateless in UAE, claimant would lack full citizenship rights if returned
propositions.quote: As a stateless person in United Arab Emirates, if he were to return, he would not have full rights of citizenship.

propositions.text: 2009 US Dept of State report notes Bidoon births registered but citizenship not granted, with discrimination and restricted movement
propositions.quote: I note from the 2009 US Department of State Report:8 The government registered Bidoon births but did not grant citizenship to the children... Without passports or other identity documents, their movement was restricted, both within the country and internationally.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes claimant's statelessness in UAE and cites 2009 US report on Bidoon discrimination and restricted movement.

propositions.text: Claimant would face some discrimination in UAE but it does not amount to persecution
propositions.quote: I find the claimant would experience some discrimination in UAE, but the foregoing does not reach the threshold of persecution.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant would face discrimination in UAE but not persecution.

propositions.text: No objective basis for claim; no serious possibility of persecution in UAE; claimant not a Convention refugee
propositions.quote: I find there is no objective basis to this claim. Therefore, I find that there is not a serious possibility or reasonable chance that the claimant would face persecution for a Convention ground, if he returns to United Arab Emirates, and he is not a Convention refugee.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimant is not a Convention refugee due to no serious risk of persecution in UAE.

propositions.text: Claimant is not a person in need of protection under Section 97 as removal to UAE poses no personal risk of life or cruel treatment
propositions.quote: I also considered Section 97 and determine that the claimant is not a person in need of protection, in that removal to United Arab Emirates would not subject him personally to a risk to his life, or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment, or a danger of torture for the same reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant not in need of protection under Section 97 as removal to UAE poses no personal risk.

propositions.text: Claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection; claim rejected
propositions.quote: Having considered all of the evidence and based on the foregoing analysis, I find the claimant, XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, not to be a Convention refugee and not to be a person in need of protection. Therefore, the Refugee Protection Division rejects his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects claimant's claim, finding him neither a Convention refugee nor in need of protection.

propositions.text: Despite claim rejection, case may warrant humanitarian and compassionate consideration if claimant cannot return to UAE
propositions.quote: Notwithstanding that the claim has been rejected, this is a case that may warrant humanitarian and compassionate consideration, if the claimant is unable to return to United Arab Emirates.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the case may warrant humanitarian and compassionate consideration despite claim rejection.
